methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 5 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Innoviz Technologies (INVZ) operates in the Drones & Autonomous sector as a public company. The comparable universe for valuation consists of five private peers: Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Elroy Air. No public peers exist within the narrow Drones & Autonomous category, limiting the applicability of traditional public market multiples.

The peer-median method was deemed inapplicable due to insufficient filtered datapoints. While five same-sector peers exist, none met the requisite filtering criteria across same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier classifications. Applying an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given the heterogeneous business models and capital requirements across broader drone and autonomous systems markets. This filtering constraint left no triangulation methods with sufficient quantitative support.

Given these data limitations, a reliable valuation range cannot be established from the provided information. The analysis is constrained by the absence of public comparables and the inability to construct a sufficiently homogeneous private peer set. Any valuation conclusion would require either (1) expansion of the peer set to include adjacent sectors with comparable technology or go-to-market characteristics, (2) direct access to financial metrics (revenue, EBITDA, growth rates) for the five identified private peers, or (3) reliance on transaction multiples or recent funding round data. The current dataset supports only the identification of structural limitations rather than a defensible valuation estimate.
